correctness.rationale: Assessment of the delivered replacement repairs/3/RESULT.md. The frozen Finding is true, but the frozen proof at line 40 states an incorrect exact one-marker minimum on middle-gap deletion. For a=c=2,b=1, deleting the middle zero loses no one-marker pattern of length 3; the first has length 4. The replacement proves the exact minimum b+1+min(a,c) by observing that loss from the union of rectangles requires u=a+b or v=b+c, and both respective axis points attain those lengths. This supplies precisely the lower bound needed when the two-marker witness has length b+2, so the global witness formula and Finding are unchanged. The published deletion and binary identity give h=1+max lambda_i against all competitors, not only equal-length words. Taking minima with the all-zero witness and then maxima with the marker-deletion witness gives the disjoint gap strata, including the special b=1 case. Their exact polynomial sums to the stated cubic at z=1. The uniform weak compositions converge by simplex Riemann sums, the boundary has probability O(1/n), and inclusion–exclusion yields the stated limit and moments by tail integration. Replay: python3 /workspace/independent_checks.py 3 uses independently generated sets of subsequences of explicit insertions for 220 words, checks 100 coefficients, and verifies the precise counterexample to the frozen proof sentence. Frozen checker and verification were inspected, not executed. The replacement also corrects citations and delimits the contribution; the frozen files were not changed.

evidence: General algorithms compute h and rho on arbitrary individual words, including binary words represented by their runs. They do not give a joint bounded-height and length polynomial.

The isolated-marker proof uses all t markers to pin each gap and positive gaps to obtain the requisite alternating subsequences on each side of an insertion. No step of that argument needs t>=3 for positive gaps, but positivity is used and cannot just be dropped.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Credit the direct extension to t=2 on the positive interior. A wordwise algorithm, or the explicit formula for all-positive gaps, is not a complete expression for the finite census where gaps can vanish.

evidence: The alternate proof for positive gaps gives h=3+max(a,b,c) at two markers, hence S_(H-3)^3 and the three-coordinate broken-stick limit. Zero gaps are negligible asymptotically but not for exact counting.

When b=0 with a,c positive the height becomes max(a,c)+2; with b=1 and precisely one positive outer gap d it becomes d+2; for b>=2 and one outer gap it becomes max(b+2,d+3). These are genuinely different active witness regimes.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: No examined earlier theorem or the overlapping same-day proof produces the missing boundary corrections by substitution. Computational evaluation of a wordwise formula on all triples does not give the exact symbolic census. The repaired result adds the vanishing-gap regimes and their combined finite polynomial, not a new asymptotic mechanism.

evidence: The audited statistic is singleton Simon-class height among all binary words. The deletion/minimality-index and insertion characterizations are known equivalent ways to compute it.

The fixed-content class census uses a related invariant, but rules out neither longer competitors nor a change of marker count at a general depth. The isolated-marker record uses the same height but only all-positive gaps and formally at least three markers.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An equal-content singleton is not a singleton among all words. Neither changing coordinates on fixed-content classes nor treating the known witness formulas as a new definition gives the claimed full census.

evidence: The four-run catalogue item gives a square length polynomial for a different run class, not a table of singleton heights for arbitrary two-one words. The two-marker congruence catalogue fixes content and counts equivalence classes. The isolated-marker item gives a positive-composition census whose extension contributes S_(H-3)^3 here.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Actual close census entries match only subfamilies or a different equivalence problem. The remaining finite terms are not supplied by those entries.

originality.rationale: Best of current knowledge, the supported distinct claim is the complete two-one length-by-height census including every vanishing-gap stratum. The proof of the same-day isolated-marker result applies at t=2 for positive gaps without a new idea, despite its formally stated t>=3 hypothesis; that fact covers the interior term and implies the same limiting distribution via the negligible boundary probability. The repaired text credits this substantive overlap and does not claim separate novelty for the limit or known height machinery. Shared date does not establish priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed complete census or a stronger enumeration with a marker-count variable could imply the remaining terms; the searches were bounded. The relative priority of the two same-day records is not established.

value.rationale: The two-marker family is the first fixed-weight setting with three interacting zero gaps. Its bounded-height distribution is an exact calibration case for singleton-language complexity. In fixed-length or cumulative counts, vanishing gaps cannot be discarded: their cumulative correction to the positive-gap count is 3H^2-11H+16 at z=1, and their distinct witness regimes determine small-height and boundary coefficients. This is useful as a complete finite reference even after crediting the positive interior and its classical broken-stick limit; it is not justified by a new proof of that limit alone.
